item.content:encoded:
The 70th Balon d'Or Ceremony took place on 26th December in London, the first time outside Paris (except for 2010-2015 in Switzerland when it merged with the FIFA awards) in commemoration of its first winner, Englishman Sir Stanley Matthews.

The award originally eligible for only European players who played for European clubs, it was expanded in 1995 to include players from any nationality who played in European clubs. The same year, saw Liberia's former President George Opong Weah pick up the award following his move from PSG to AC Milan.

This year's format saw a set of journalists, one from each of the FIFA top-ranked 100 nations of the world vote for the best player who had distinguished himself from August 2025-July 2026. The criteria was based on individual performances, team play/collective trophies and fair play.

30 names were compiled with the journalists voting for their top 10 via a point-based system: 1st - 15 points, 2nd -12 points, 3rd - 10 points, 4th - 8 points, 5th - 7 points, 6th - 5 points, 7th - 4 points, 8th - 3 points, 9th - 2 points & 10th - 1 point.

Harry Kane got the Golden Ball, the first for an Englishman in 25 years after Michael Owen (following Liverpool's League Cup, UEFA Cup & FA Cup triumphs) in 2001.

Mbappe & Yamal finished 2nd & 3rd respectively.

item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Police Command has rescued three young girls from a suspected human trafficking operation in Badagry, Lagos State.

The girls were reportedly being transported on a commercial motorcycle when police officers intercepted the rider during a routine patrol.

The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed the incident in a statement shared on Friday.

According to the police spokesperson, officers intercepted the motorcycle along Owode Apa Road in Badagry. Three young girls were found on the motorcycle.

Police interrogation reportedly revealed that the girls were victims of human trafficking.

The officers rescued the girls and conducted an initial debriefing. The police said efforts were ongoing to identify and arrest the suspected traffickers.

The case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Panti, Yaba, for further investigation.

The police have not disclosed the identities or ages of the rescued girls. Details about where they were allegedly being taken, who arranged their movement and whether any suspect has been arrested were also not provided in the report.

The rescue has again drawn attention to the need for stronger action against human trafficking and the protection of vulnerable children.

Authorities are expected to establish how the girls were recruited, who was responsible for transporting them and whether other people were involved in the suspected operation.

The investigation will be important in identifying those responsible and preventing further exploitation.

item.title: Sam Amadi: When Intellectualism Surrenders To Partisanship - Dan Nwomeh - Politics
item.description: <div><div>Given his well-known status as a public intellectual, I was taken aback to read Dr. Sam Amadi's article, Peter Mbah Is Failing, and Failing Unnecessarily. item.content:encoded:
Given his well-known status as a public intellectual, I was taken aback to read Dr. Sam Amadi's article, Peter Mbah Is Failing, and Failing Unnecessarily. It was filled with intellectual dishonesty, extreme partisanship, unsubstantiated allegations, emotionally charged and incendiary rhetoric, spurious statistical interpretations, and a disturbing disregard for research and scholarship. What purported to be objective political analysis was, in reality, an exercise in partisan rabble-rousing, emotion-stirring and pandering to his well-known political constituency. @SamAmadi is no longer the intellectual we used to know.

Consider his preposterous claim that somebody is shot dead at a political rally in Enugu every week. What a reckless and irresponsible assertion! Where are the names of the victims, dates, locations and police records? How did he arrive at this conclusion? This is a state that security experts have consistently identified as having one of the lowest crime rates in Nigeria, with independent assessments indicating a reduction of more than 80 per cent in violent crime since Mbah assumed office in 2023.Regular attacks and violent incidents occur in other states, including Imo and Abia, yet Amadi conveniently applies an entirely different standard to Enugu.

Indeed, Enugu has invested in one of Nigeria's most sophisticated security architectures, featuring thousands of AI-enabled surveillance cameras, drones, nearly 200 patrol vehicles equipped with intelligent cameras and a Command and Control Centre providing real-time monitoring. The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, recently commended the facility and urged other states to understudy it. It is rated as the most advanced such facilities in the country and an outstanding security investment in the South East. These investments do not make crime impossible, but they make a mockery of the suggestion that the state is indifferent to security. Amadi should interrogate actual security data rather than fabricating a weekly killing statistic.

His economic analysis is equally embarrassing. He repeatedly presents Enugu's impressive IGR growth as evidence that Governor Mbah is extracting more taxes from a relatively less productive economy. Has he bothered to examine the composition of that revenue? The 2025 figures, publicly available at the click of a button, show that tax revenue accounted for just ₦51.5 billion, or 12.6 per cent, of Enugu's ₦406.77 billion IGR. The remaining ₦355.2 billion, representing 87.4 per cent, came from non-tax sources, principally the recovery, revitalisation and commercial optimisation of previously moribund state-owned assets. Technology-driven revenue tracking, electronic payments and the plugging of leakages have also transformed collections. The days of indiscriminate cash collection have been replaced by traceable electronic platforms. How did Amadi arrive at the conclusion that this represents excessive taxation? He has confused revenue mobilisation with taxation and then built an indictment on that confusion. This is a disappointing failure of intellectual rigour expected of the Amadi we used to know. His pronouncement on Enugu's GDP performance is similarly unsupported. He offers no dataset, reporting period or methodology, yet speaks with such astonishing authority.

On political pluralism, nobody should excuse intimidation or violence against opposition supporters. Every incident deserves impartial investigation and prosecution where culpability is established. But allegations are not convictions, and political incidents do not automatically establish gubernatorial sponsorship. Even the Amadeo controversy must be examined in light of the management’s own account. Management explained that the booking was made by a charity organisation for a purpose different from the political gathering the organisers subsequently sought to hold.

The organisation, it emerged, was dishonestly fronting for the NDC. Management also expressly denied that its decision was taken on the instructions of the Enugu State Government. Amadi conveniently disregards this account while alleging government interference, despite the management’s explicit denial of any such involvement. He cannot transform every allegation into proof of a state-sponsored campaign of terror.

The fact that he encountered some political support groups at one summit in Owerri does not constitute a credible basis for judging the comparative democratic credentials of four states. A credible assessment demands consistent standards of evidence, not sweeping conclusions drawn from an isolated personal experience.

Equally disingenuous is his attempt to ethnicise political disagreement. Enugu does not become less Igbo because its governor belongs to APC or supports President Tinubu. Nor does an Enugu citizen surrender his Igbo identity by supporting APC. Igbo identity is not the exclusive property of Peter Obi, his supporters or any political tendency. Ndi Enugu are entitled to make their political choices without ethnic intimidation or accusations of betrayal.

Amadi's intolerance of criticism of Obi is also becoming difficult to ignore. Anyone who questions Obi's political (mis)calculations risks being cast as an enemy of the Igbo. He attacked Governor Soludo for criticising Obi. Now Mbah is subjected to the same vicious treatment. The politics of grievance, protest, lamentation and self-isolation has done Ndigbo no favours. The most important objective of any patriotic Igbo politician should be to relaunch our people into the heart of Nigerian politics and the inner circle of power where decisions shaping our collective destiny are made. Obi cannot be allowed to drag the entire Igbo political class into the ocean in pursuit of his personal ambition.

Amadi, who contested for the governorship of his home state of Imo under the Labour Party in 2023 but failed to secure the party’s ticket, is now aligned with Obi’s faction of the NDC. He is entitled to his political preferences, but he must not disguise partisanship as scholarship. Defending democracy requires intellectual honesty, rigorous engagement with facts, consistency in the application of standards, respect for opposing views, and a willingness to rise above partisan interests, rather than resorting to sensationalism, ethnic manipulation and divisive rhetoric. Ndi Enugu are indeed not zombies, and they need no intellectual gatekeepers to dictate their political choices. The right to disagree with Governor Mbah must be protected, just as the right to support him must be respected. That is what pluralism actually means.

item.title: NHIA Union Issues 7-Day Ultimatum to Management Over Staff Welfare - Career
item.description:
Tension is mounting at the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) as the National Union of Banks, Insurance and Financial Institutions Employees (NUBIFIE) has issued a seven-day ultimatum to the management to reverse the transfer of its chairman and address concerns over staff welfare.

The union threatened to embark on lawful industrial action if the management fails to comply with its demands, raising fears of a possible industrial dispute that could disrupt ac...
item.content:encoded:
Tension is mounting at the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) as the National Union of Banks, Insurance and Financial Institutions Employees (NUBIFIE) has issued a seven-day ultimatum to the management to reverse the transfer of its chairman and address concerns over staff welfare.

The union threatened to embark on lawful industrial action if the management fails to comply with its demands, raising fears of a possible industrial dispute that could disrupt activities at the health insurance agency.

The ultimatum followed months of alleged neglect of workers’ welfare concerns, unsuccessful attempts to secure meetings with management, and claims of intimidation and victimisation of staff who speak out against policies considered unfavourable to employees.

In a letter reportedly addressed to the NHIA management, the union’s national leadership demanded the immediate and unconditional reversal of the transfer of the NUBIFIE chairman from the authority’s Abuja headquarters to Kano.

The union reportedly viewed the transfer as an attempt to weaken its leadership and discourage workers from pressing for improved conditions of service.

When contacted to confirm the development, the chairman of NUBIFIE’s NHIA Domestic Unit acknowledged that welfare-related issues existed within the authority but declined further comment, saying the union’s national leadership had taken over the matter.

A senior officer at the authority’s headquarters in Abuja, who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the matter, alleged that staff had become increasingly apprehensive about speaking openly on their concerns for fear of victimisation or transfer.

The officer questioned the disparity between the Federal Government’s minimum wage increase and the salary adjustment reportedly granted to NHIA workers.

“How can the Federal Government increase the minimum wage by 133 per cent and then you give us a paltry 30 per cent in the authority after 12 years, given the prevailing harsh economic condition in the country and the present tax regime?” the officer asked.

The officer also alleged that the management had introduced or maintained policies detrimental to staff welfare, including prolonged stagnation in career progression, discontinuation of disengagement allowances, suspension of staff capacity-building training and delays in the payment of allowances.

Another staff member familiar with the situation said workers were struggling to meet basic financial obligations, including transportation costs, children’s school fees and house rent.

“Yes, it is true that NHIA staff are seriously suffering. Staff cannot meet basic needs such as transportation, payment of children’s school fees and house rent. Even the directors are just suffering and smiling,” the staff member said.

The staff member also raised concerns about the absence of a formal Condition of Service, which employees believe should provide clear guidelines on promotions, allowances, welfare entitlements and protection against arbitrary management decisions.

“Will you believe that this organisation does not have a Condition of Service? We are just on auto-pilot,” the staff member said.

The workers’ grievances also extend to what they described as the growing reliance on external consultants since the appointment of Dr Kelechi Ohiri as Director-General of the NHIA in 2023.

According to the allegations, consultants were being engaged and paid while experienced in-house personnel were increasingly sidelined, despite their institutional knowledge and technical expertise.

The development has raised concerns among staff about career progression, recognition of professional competence and the role of experienced employees in implementing the authority’s mandate.

The dispute comes at a critical time for the health insurance agency, which plays a major role in the implementation of the Federal Government’s health sector reforms under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative (NHSRII), part of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The aggrieved workers argued that the success of the government’s health sector renewal programme depends partly on the welfare, motivation and capacity of personnel responsible for implementing its policies.

They maintained that poor working conditions could undermine staff morale and affect service delivery if the grievances were not urgently addressed.

The union’s intervention at the national level is expected to intensify pressure on the management to engage workers’ representatives and resolve the dispute before it escalates.

NUBIFIE reportedly warned that failure to meet its demands within the stipulated seven days would compel it to mobilise members across the country for lawful industrial action to protect workers’ rights and welfare.

The union’s ultimatum has now placed the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment and other relevant authorities under pressure to intervene and prevent a possible breakdown of industrial relations at the agency.

While the workers insist that their demands are rooted in legitimate welfare concerns, the NHIA management is yet to publicly respond to the allegations contained in the claims made available to our correspondent.

item.content:encoded:
URGENT PUBLIC STATEMENT ON THE DISAPPEARANCE OF IMRAN (@IU_WAKILII)

I make this statement with deep concern as Imran's fellow colleague, associate in the El-Rufa'i Camp, and Convener of the El-Rufa'i Youth Movement.

Yesterday, Imran sent me a statement and specifically requested that I make it public if we became unable to reach him or establish his whereabouts. In keeping with his request, I am making the statement public.

It has now been over 12 hours since I last spoke with Imran. Despite several attempts by members of the El-Rufa'i Camp youth to reach him, all efforts have been unsuccessful.

We are deeply concerned about his safety and whereabouts.

I appeal to the general public and security agencies to assist us in locating him. Anyone with useful information should contact:

X: @ElRufai_Live / @ElrufaiBoys
Email: elrufailive@gmail.com
Phone: +234 808 213 1009

Below is the statement Imran sent to me yesterday, which he requested I publish if we could not find him.

We want to know that Imran is safe. Please help amplify this message.

Signed:
Convener, El-Rufa'i Youth Movement

Imran's statement

"Earlier today, police personnel came to my house looking for me, but unfortunately, I was not around. They told those they met that the matter was urgent and that I needed to report to them. However, I was occupied at the time and could not immediately attend to their request.

After a while, they left, and I thought that was all for the moment. After a while they returned and this time, the situation took a different turn.

When they came back, they arrested my younger brother and towed my car. According to them, I had to present myself before they could release him. The reason they gave was that the car I have been driving for over two years was allegedly a stolen vehicle.

What makes this situation particularly surprising to me is that before I started using the car, my brother has been using it for atleast two to three years. In other words, this is not a vehicle that either of us started using yesterday. Yet, I am now faced with an allegation that has resulted in the arrest of my younger brother.

I am making this public because I am on my way to meet the police now. I believe it is important that people are aware of the situation, particularly because my brother has been arrested in connection with a matter they say concerns me.

I will be going there to understand exactly what is happening and to find out the basis of this allegation.

For now, I do not want to jump to conclusions or make claims about what I do not yet know.

I will provide further updates as the situation unfolds.

Thank you.

Signed Imran U Wakili"

item.content:encoded:
Major anti-government protests sweep across Italy
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FOFt2Qqxlx8?si=KXsdYWEueBkQPNe2

Demonstrators wave flags and shout slogans through megaphones during a nationwide general strike called by grassroots unions to protest rising living costs, low wages and military spending in Rome, Friday, Oct. 30.
Demonstrators wave flags and shout slogans

Farmers dumped manure on the streets of Turin on Friday as mass demonstrations unfurled across more than 50 cities in Italy.

Fired up by a wave of similar protests elsewhere in Europe, tens of thousands of Italians took to the streets to protest soaring living costs and the poor state of public services such as healthcare and education.

Friday’s nationwide action was spearheaded by the anti-capitalist trade union Unione Sindacale di Base (USB), and included workers across the public and private sectors.

Transport workers had been slated to join the pickets too, but abandoned plans after Transport Minister Matteo Salvini threatened the sector with sanctions. The USB urged taxi drivers to go ahead with strikes, despite them receiving a similar warning.

The largest rallies took place in Milan, Turin and the capital of Rome, where young and old united to vent their anger at Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and her right-wing government.

Demonstrators in Milan held placards bearing anti-government slogans, “Let’s oust the Meloni government—rebellion is just,” one read. In Naples, some protesters burnt photos of Meloni.

Italy’s Interior Ministry said “preventative” arrests were made ahead of the marches to quell violence. Apart from a few isolated skirmishes, the demonstrations were largely peaceful as they continued into the afternoon.

When some youngsters in Rome tried to set a dumpster on fire, others quickly extinguished the blaze, keen to avoid the type of violence that has marred similar protests in France.

A strong anti-war sentiment was in evidence, with many protesters waving Palestinian flags as they marched. Others held banners opposing the government’s military spending.

While Friday’s industrial action has been nationwide, demands have varied from one location to the next.

In the northern city of Genoa, dockworkers mobilized against the “militarization” of the port in a bid to block the export of Italian-made arm shipments to conflict zones, including Israel.

But in nearby Bologna, students called on the government to review education policy.

Protests have swept through Europe in recent weeks as hundreds of thousands of people have demanded government action to ease the rising cost of living.

Demonstrations in France began in late September with teachers and students protesting a lack of investment in education and woeful working conditions. The protests have since escalated to reflect wider cost-of-living concerns .

A deepening housing crisis has triggered demonstrations across Spain and Portugal, with activists erecting encampments in the capitals’ central plazas.

Albania has seen a series of anti-government protests, with thousands taking to the streets to highlight alleged government corruption and to demand the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

And in Serbia, youth protests were effective in ousting long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić last weekend.

item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Kidnappers Hold Two Sons Of Nigerian Military Officer For Nine Weeks, Demand Fresh N200m After Collecting N26m, 25 Phones

Two young sons of a Nigerian Air Force personnel have spent nine weeks in the custody of kidnappers in Kaduna State, with their captors now demanding a fresh N200 million ransom after the family had already paid N26 million and handed over 25 mobile phones, their mother has told SaharaReporters.

Tina Daniel Dominic, whose husband is an Air Force officer, said her sons, Derrick, who will turns 14 in December, and Damian, 12, were abducted from their home at Rimi, Kamazou, in the Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, on Sunday, August 30, 2026, when gunmen broke into the house at night.

The mother, who spoke to SaharaReporters on Friday, said the family had sold their cars and other valuables to raise the first N20 million, and had also bought 25 mobile phones for the abductors, yet the children remain in captivity.

Recounting the night of the abduction, Mrs Dominic said she was unwell and had gone to bed earlier than usual when she began hearing gunshots.

“On 30th of August, 2026, I was in my home at Rimi, Kamazou. That night, I was not feeling fine, so we entered earlier than usual. We were sleeping, and then I started hearing noise, sounds of gunshots,” she said.

“So I picked my phone to call my neighbour, I’m hearing gunshots. They said yes, that it’s close, but they heard that kidnappers were in my neighbour’s house.

“I now wake up, on my way to go and wake my children to come so that we can stay together. I now realise that they are in my house. I was hearing how they were trying to break my fence.”

She said her husband, an Air Force personnel, was away at his place of work at the time.

“My husband is an Air Force personnel. He went back to his place of work,” she said.

“So I hid my children inside my kitchen pantry. Even before I finished hiding them, they had already come in through my first son’s room, Derrick’s room. They opened the burglary and came in.

“I’ve already hidden my three children, Derrick, Damian and Dominion.

”

The gunmen, she said, demanded to know where her husband and the children were. She told them the children had gone to their father for the holiday, but they refused to believe her.

“They start pointing guns in my head, and they started asking me to open doors and they start checking. Then they took me outside, tied my hands, and took me outside.

“On reaching outside my house, to my other neighbour’s house, I saw my other neighbour already tied there.”

She said the abductors kept going back and forth between her house and where she was held, insisting she was lying about the whereabouts of her children.

“They said I should not lie to them, that they know everything. I should not lie, that they know my children are in the house. That I should not lie. And my husband, I said no, my husband left late. They were asking, if I do not tell the truth, they will kill me.

“I insisted that my children are not around, but they went in and came back. I think they received a call that the children are in the house. So they went back to the house, and then the only thing I saw, they brought my two sons out.

“I was asking Derrick, why did you people come out? They said, ‘No mommy, we did not come out, they opened and they checked and they saw us.’ I said where is Dominion, they said they left Dominion.”

Mrs Dominic said the gunmen marched her, her two sons and a neighbour through the bush for about two hours before deciding she was too weak to continue.

“We walked to an extent with the children and my neighbour. We followed the back of that Rimi. We are walking and along the line, like an hour to two hours’ walk, they saw that I could not go on again because I was falling, I could not walk faster. I was falling because I was not feeling fine.

“So they said I should go back. I said I cannot go back, where will I go? They said no, I should go back and look for money. And then they collected my phone and said I should go back and look for money, that they will call back.

“I said I don’t know the road of that location. They said I should go back, that I should just be going, that I will see people. So that is how I managed to reach home that day.”

Ransom: From N500 Million to N20 Million, Then N6 Million And Still No Release

The next day, she said, the kidnappers made contact and demanded N500 million.

“I reached home, and then the next day they contacted us to say that we pay N500 million. My husband told them we don’t have N500 million. That he is a soldier. They said he is a very rich soldier, he flies airplane. My husband told them no, he doesn’t fly planes. They insisted and said we bring the money.

“So we started going back and forth. They now said N100 million again. After a week, we came down to N100 million. We said we cannot afford N100 million. Then after some days, they said N20 million. That it is N20 million, they are going to collect last, that they are not removing one naira.”

She said the family agreed and began selling their belongings.

“We had to sell our cars to try to raise that N20 million and other valuables. We raised the N20 million, they took the 20 million to them. After taking the 20 million, we were expecting they will release our children.

“The way they took money from our neighbour, I think about N15 million thereabouts, and they released him. So we thought after we give the money, they will release the children. They did not release the children.

“In fact, they stopped calling us for like a wek. After a week, they started calling again. We said they haven’t released the children. They said no, that the money we took to them is not complete. They said that about N1.3 million is missing from the money. Tomorrow they will say N1.5 million. Next day, they will say N3 million. They are just going up and down.

“Later, they now said we should bring another N6 million. And they gave the children phone to talk to us, that if we bring the money, they are going to release them.”

She said a released captive assured the family that the children would be freed once the additional N6 million was paid.

“Somebody in the camp that they released, they talked to that person, and the woman assured us that after we give that money, they said they are going to release the children. She heard them saying this.

“So we started looking for another N6 million and giving to them again. They still did not release the children. With other things we took to them; we took phones, like 25 phones to them. They still did not release the children.”

New Demand: N200 Million After Two Weeks of Silence

Mrs Dominic said the abductors stopped calling for two weeks before reaching out again on Thursday, October 29, with a fresh demand, this time for N200 million, claiming her husband had sent people to their camp.

“Yesterday, being 29th of October, they reached out to us and said that my husband is a military officer, that he sent people to come to their camp, that they took some people from their camp. So for that, they are not releasing the children. That we have to bring N200 million. That is the new development, that we have to bring N200 million before they will release the children, which we don’t have.

“We are crying to the government. We don’t have that amount of money to give to them. We say we don’t have. They said we should go to the government. That my husband is a government worker, that we should go, they will help us. We say we don’t have. That there is no way we can raise that amount of money.

“And since two weeks, they have not talked to us.”

The distraught mother said she had repeatedly posted about the abduction on social media and tagged the Kaduna State Governor and President Bola Tinubu, but no government official had reached out to the family.

“We are crying for help from anywhere and everywhere to secure the release of my children. The government has abandoned us. I posted the kidnap incident and tagged the Kaduna State Governor and President Bola Tinubu, but it appears nobody is interested in our case.

“We are being tortured because my husband is a Nigerian military officer. For two weeks now I have been writing and posting, tagging government officials, but no one has reached out.”

She said her children are young and one of them is in fragile health.

“I’m begging, these children are small. By December, Derrick will be 14 years, while Damian is 12 years. Damian was not strong; he had a major surgery about two years ago, and recently he came back from school and we were supposed to go to the hospital the next day, being Monday, before this incident happened on Sunday for his check-up.

“My husband is a military officer who leaves us every now and then to save this country, but no one, including his country, is ready to save his family. The government should come to our aid. These kidnappers are asking us for what we cannot afford. We have sold everything we’ve got. We bought 25 mobile phones for them, yet they are asking for another N200 million.

“I am begging the Kaduna State Government to come to our aid. As a mother, I’m begging that this situation should touch those in authority, unless they are part of the kidnapping gang. For nine weeks now, these children have been held in captivity,” she lamented.

SaharaReporters had previously reported that two children of the brother-in-law of Gurara TV Chief Executive Officer and APM candidate for the Jema’a/Sanga Federal Constituency, Ernest Thyek Maidawa, were kidnapped and had remained in captivity for two months.

The children were reportedly abducted from their residence in the Rimi area of Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, the same area where Mrs Dominic’s sons were taken.

The incident has continued to raise concerns among relatives, residents and community members, particularly over the prolonged period the victims have spent in captivity.

The development comes amid persistent concerns over kidnapping and other forms of insecurity across parts of Kaduna State, with families frequently forced to negotiate with criminals following abductions.

Obasanjo Blasts Tinubu Over Borrowing, Says ‘It’s Absolute Nonsense’ by SeeHim(op): 9:07pm On Oct 30
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his comment that borrowing is not leprosy, describing the position as “absolute nonsense”.

Obasanjo spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum theme “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate National Development.”

In April, Tinubu said his administration would continue to borrow whenever necessary, insisting that it should not be viewed negatively.

Tinubu spoke at the State House during a meeting with Plateau leaders led by Caleb Mutfwang, the governor, and Nentawe Yilwatda, national chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC). “If we have to borrow, we borrow.

Borrowing is not leprosy, we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the president had said. His remarks came amid rising public concern over Nigeria’s growing debt burden and the increasing share of national revenue committed to debt servicing.

Re: Obasanjo Blasts Tinubu Over Borrowing, Says ‘It’s Absolute Nonsense’ by malali: 2:22am

Obasanjo is absolutely right. Tinubu's statement that borrowing is not leprosy is an astonishingly shallow response to a national economic catastrophe. The real question is not whether borrowing is acceptable; it is what Nigeria is borrowing for, what value it creates, and who will ultimately pays.

Tinubu is behaving like an economic hitman sent to mortgage Nigeria's future on behalf of powerful external interests. He is borrowing without demonstrating a credible, comprehensive plan for economic recovery. Debt without productive investment is simply intergenerational economic sabotage.

Nigerians have sacrificed everything this administration demanded: petrol subsidy, foreign exchange support, purchasing power and their standard of living. Yet where are the dividends? Despite periods of exceptionally high oil prices, Nigerians are drowning in inflation, unbearable petrol costs and collapsing disposable incomes. Petrol can cost more than an ordinary worker earns in a month!

Buhari governed through a global pandemic and periods of oil prices around $30 per barrel. That does not excuse his failures, but it makes the present administration's inability to translate economic reforms and oil revenues into tangible improvements even harder to defend.

There is no convincing economic blueprint, no visible social dividend and no credible explanation of when ordinary Nigerians will begin to benefit from their sacrifices. Instead, we see an increasingly detached political elite, lavish political entourages, endless borrowing and religious symbolism being deployed in an environment where economic accountability should be paramount.

At this point, Tinubu appears dangerously out of his depth. His economic decisions are beginning to look less like a coherent recovery strategy and more like an exercise in dismantling the country's economic foundations. Nigerians should not have to mortgage generations yet unborn to finance a government that cannot convincingly explain what it is building.

A country is not governed by borrowing money. It is governed by knowing what to do with it. And Nigeria deserves considerably more than slogans, debt and demands for patience.

Why Are Male Nurses Banned From Labour Wards? - Nigerian Nurse Raises Alarm by Historyrewrites(op): 8:33pm On Oct 30

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbUcaKQEdVI
Nigerian Nurse Questions Why Male Nurses Are Denied Access to Labour Wards

A Nigerian male nurse has sparked an online debate after questioning why male nurses are reportedly prevented from entering labour wards in some hospitals while male doctors are allowed to attend to women during childbirth.

In a video shared online, the nurse expressed frustration over the practice, claiming that even male nursing interns are sometimes denied access to labour wards despite needing practical experience as part of their training.

He questioned the apparent double standard, arguing that male nurses should not be excluded from clinical training opportunities simply because of their gender.

The nurse also criticised senior nursing personnel and hospital administrators who allegedly enforce the restrictions, urging male nurses to familiarise themselves with the professional guidelines of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria.

His comments have reignited conversations about gender equality in the nursing profession, professional development and the treatment of male nurses in Nigerian healthcare facilities.

However, the debate also highlights the importance of respecting patients' privacy, dignity and consent during childbirth.

The discussion has raised an important question: how can hospitals ensure equal training opportunities for male and female nurses while respecting the preferences and rights of patients?

In some parts of the world, particularly in conservative Muslim communities, there is a strong preference for female doctors, nurses and midwives to handle intimate examinations and childbirth whenever possible. What makes the situation even more puzzling is that, in medical schools there are good numbers of female students-doctors, sometimes making up 50% or more . Yet, when you visit many hospitals, male doctors seem disproportionately visible in many departments, AND EVEN MORE IN FEMALE CARE RELATED DEPARTMENTS.
Where do all the female medical graduates go after graduation Are they choosing not to practise? Are there structural barriers keeping them away? Or is something happening within the medical profession that we are not discussing?

If female doctors are being trained in such numbers, why aren't more of them visible in fields that directly concern women's reproductive health? WHAT ARE THEY DOING WITH THEIR LIVES AFTER GRADUATION?

item.content:encoded:
SoftBank-backed Nigerian fintech company OPay has raised $304 million in its initial public offering (IPO) in the United States, securing a valuation of approximately $4 billion as it seeks to expand its presence in the growing digital financial services market.

The fintech firm, which focuses on Nigeria and other emerging markets, sold 16 million American depositary shares at $19 each, according to a report by Reuters on Friday.

The offering price was at the lower end of its targeted range of $19 to $21 per share.

OPay’s listing comes amid challenging market conditions, with persistent inflation and a selloff in artificial intelligence-related stocks weighing on investor sentiment.

The uncertainty has prompted several companies to postpone their planned listings as market volatility and concerns over valuations make it increasingly difficult to attract investors and secure favourable pricing.

Founded in 2018, OPay provides digital financial services across emerging markets, including Nigeria and Indonesia.

Its platform offers payments, money transfers, savings and loans through a single application, targeting gaps in banking infrastructure and limited access to traditional financial services in developing economies.

The company was founded by Chinese billionaire Yahui Zhou, who also established Beijing Kunlun Tech, a Chinese gaming company that previously owned dating application Grindr.

OPay previously raised $400 million in 2021 at a valuation of $2 billion, marking a significant increase in its valuation ahead of its latest public offering.

According to its IPO prospectus, the fintech company had approximately 50 million monthly active users as of July 31, 2026.

SoftBank entities held a 6.6 per cent stake in OPay before the public offering, according to the filing.

Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, Standard Bank and CICC are among the underwriters managing the IPO.

Following the offering, OPay is expected to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol OPAY.

item.content:encoded:
Police have arrested two Nigerian nationals and recovered mephedrone and cocaine collectively valued at Rs 2.2 crore from them in Maharashtra’s Thane district, an official said on Friday.

The operation was carried out on Wednesday by the Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) of the Navi Mumbai police with assistance from the Mumbra police in the Diva-Mumbra area.

According to senior inspector Sandeep Nigade from ANC, they arrested two Nigerians, identified as Akuba Kenneth (45) and Sunday Eze (47), as part of an investigation in a drug case registered at the Taloja police station in Navi Mumbai.

The operation involving over two dozen police personnel led to the seizure of over 2 kg of mephedrone, 316.5 grams of cocaine and six mobile phones used by the accused. The narcotic substances are worth about Rs 2.2 crore, he said.

Nine persons, including five African nationals, have been arrested in connection with the Navi Mumbai case so far, the official said, adding that further probe is underway.

item.content:encoded:
Peter Obi will crash dollar to N500, slash bread to N800, rice to N27,500 if elected — Pat Utomi vows

Political economist Pat Utomi has said the presidential campaign of Peter Obi and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is proposing to strengthen the naira to N500 against the dollar if elected in 2027.

Utomi disclosed this in a post on X, explaining that the exchange-rate target forms part of the party’s economic blueprint aimed at tackling inflation, reducing poverty and restoring Nigerians’ purchasing power.

According to him, the proposed naira appreciation would be supported by investments in security, electricity and road infrastructure, as well as structural reforms designed to make the economy more competitive.

He projected that the plan could trigger significant reductions in the prices of essential commodities.

Under the proposed programme, a loaf of sliced bread currently selling for about N1,750 could fall to N800, while a 50kg bag of imported rice could drop from N55,000 to N27,500.

A medium-sized yam, he said, could reduce from N2,400 to N1,200, while a 50kg bag of maize could decline from N75,000 to N37,500. Plantain could fall from N2,500 to N1,250, while a whole chicken could drop from N7,000 to N3,500.

Utomi also projected that a dozen eggs could sell for N1,150 instead of N2,300, while a painter of garri could drop from N1,300 to N650. He added that petrol and cement would also become cheaper.

“We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he said.

“It offers a direct, multi-faceted approach to curbing inflation, reducing poverty, and lowering the cost of living.”

Utomi added that the proposal represents the party’s “concrete plan to uplift the 140 million Nigerians currently experiencing multi-dimensional poverty.”

However, he did not state when the N500/$ target would be achieved or provide details of the monetary and fiscal measures required to sustain such an appreciation.

A 15-year-old Ghanaian boy, identified as Javits Frimpong, has died after being shot while reportedly on his way to school in the Bronx, New York.

The incident occurred around 9:30 a.m. on Thursday, October 29, near Crotona Park. According to police, the teenager was shot in the stomach but managed to run approximately one block before collapsing.

He was subsequently rushed to a hospital, where he later died.

Javits' father, Thomas Frimpong, believes the incident may be connected to bullying his son had reportedly experienced at school.

Speaking to ABC7 New York, the grieving father disclosed that the school's principal had informed him three days before the shooting that two students had been suspended over bullying allegations.

He described his son as a quiet, intelligent and precious child who rarely spent time outside their home.

Police are searching for three teenage suspects who reportedly fled the scene wearing black clothing and blue surgical masks. No arrests have been announced.

However, authorities have not established whether the shooting was connected to the reported bullying.

The tragic incident has sparked outrage among residents, with community members calling for stronger measures to tackle bullying and youth violence.

Investigations into the teenager's death are ongoing.

More APC-Branded SUVs Surface As Nigerians Grapple With Economic Hardship by givewotowoto2(op): 5:11pm On Oct 30

A video showing numerous APC-branded campaign SUVs parked at an undisclosed location, suspected to be in Zamfara State, has surfaced amid widespread economic hardship in Nigeria.

This comes after recent public outrage over reports that First Lady Remi Tinubu gifted SUVs allegedly worth ₦180 million each to party members, while millions of Nigerians struggle to make ends meet.

These developments reflect broader public anger and dissatisfaction with Tinubu's government over perceived wasteful spending and corruption.

In a country battling hunger and insecurity, see what First Lady is sharing to APC youths.
This is the same government that asked Nigerians to endure.
I can’t wait for us to kick out these criminals. pic.twitter.com/zpXbiDHgLt

item.content:encoded:
🇺🇸 Two U.S helicopters collided in midair near a small airport in Oregon on the afternoon of Oct. 29, killing all three people aboard and closing a nearby highway as emergency crews responded to the crash scene.

Investigators were combing through debris scattered across a field in northwest Oregon Thursday after two helicopters collided midair, killing three people and forcing the closure of a nearby highway, officials said.

Texas flight instructor Maddie Aasbo, 22, and Oregon pilot Tyler Sturdevant, 38, died in the crash as well as a student pilot from the United Kingdom, Yamhill County Sheriff Sam Elliott said during a news conference.

Aasbo was in one helicopter with the student pilot and Sturdevant was the sole occupant of the other, the sheriff said.

The aircraft crashed to the ground in a private farm field near McMinnville Municipal Airport, officials said, with a red helicopter left crumpled in pieces and a green helicopter lying upside down. McMinnville is about 40 miles southwest of Portland.

A one-mile stretch of nearby Highway 233 was closed due to the crash, the Oregon Department of Transportation said Thursday afternoon, giving no estimate for reopening.

Leo Rodriguez said he called 911 after witnessing the crash from his family vineyard.

“All of a sudden I hear this big boom and this metal breaking, and I look up and just see these two helicopters just collided in mid-air,” he told CNN affiliate KPTV.

“It took me a while, for my brain to figure out what I was seeing. You don’t see this every day. They twisted and fell to the ground.”

The sheriff’s office asked the public to avoid the area and have “patience as we respond to this critical incident.”

item.content:encoded:
yaroinsider:
African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore has spoken from a hospital after an alleged attack by armed men at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

The incident reportedly occurred around 1pm on Friday, October 30, while Sowore was in the state for political activities and engagements with party members.

Earlier, Sowore raised the alarm on social media, claiming that armed men had attacked him and members of his team inside a restaurant.

In another post, his campaign alleged that he had been abducted and that his whereabouts were unknown.

However, subsequent reports showed Sowore speaking from a hospital, where he described the incident and accused individuals linked to the Ekiti State Government House of involvement.

Sowore accuses DSS of providing support

In a statement shared on his social media account, Sowore alleged that the attackers came from the Government House and received tracking and operational support from operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS).

He also claimed that DSS operatives had been monitoring and harassing him and members of his team since their arrival in Ekiti.

These allegations have not been independently established.

The identities of the attackers and the circumstances surrounding the incident remain subjects requiring investigation.

Campaign raises alarm

The Sowore/Magashi Presidential Election Campaign described the incident as a serious security concern.

In a statement signed by campaign spokesperson Abdulkareem Musa, the campaign called on the Nigeria Police Force, DSS, Independent National Electoral Commission and other relevant authorities to investigate the incident and ensure the safety of the AAC candidate.

The campaign also condemned political violence and intimidation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Ayoyinka Oni, the campaign’s Director of Strategy, Policy and Political Affairs, told the Foundation for Investigative Journalism that Sowore had travelled to Ekiti to meet party members and participate in the Ekiti Ikogosi Marathon.

Police response awaited

The Ekiti State Police Commissioner, Falade Adegoroye Michael, reportedly visited the scene of the incident.

Sowore subsequently criticised the police response, arguing that the commissioner’s description of the incident did not reflect the seriousness of what happened.

As of the latest reports reviewed, a full account of the incident, the identities of those responsible and the outcome of any police investigation had not been established.

The Ekiti State Government and the DSS should also respond to the allegations made against them.

Questions ahead of 2027

The incident has raised concerns about the safety of political candidates and their supporters as preparations for the 2027 general elections continue.

Authorities must establish what happened at the restaurant, identify those responsible and investigate any allegation of involvement by security personnel or political actors.

Political disagreements should not expose candidates, campaign workers or ordinary citizens to violence.

Yaro Insider will continue to follow the investigation and publish verified updates as more information becomes available.

Source: https://yaroinsider.ng/sowore-hospital-after-alleged-attack-ekiti/

item.content:encoded:
PRESS STATEMENT

INEC MUST NAME REGISTER CULPRITS AND EXPOSE ELECTION CONTRACTORS

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has condemned INEC’s admission that AI generated images and other irregularities entered the voter register through registration officers, calling it a scandal that strikes at the heart of the Commission’s credibility.

In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said:

“INEC has admitted that some AI generated images are on the voter register and that registration officers introduced irregularities across the country. The Commission charged with protecting Nigerians’ votes has acknowledged that its own system was abused by those entrusted to operate it. This is a catastrophic failure of leadership and safeguards.

“Professor Joash Amupitan through Boyode Lawrence says INEC knows what its officers did and how they tampered with the register, yet claims it does not know why. That is a disgraceful evasion, not an answer. Even ordinary WhatsApp, Facebook and email accounts appear to have stronger security safeguards than those INEC’s ICT director described on national television. How can the database holding the votes of millions of Nigerians be less secure than a personal social media account?

“If INEC knows how the register was compromised, it must disclose the evidence, identify every officer involved and explain why they have not been suspended and prosecuted. Amupitan cannot admit the misconduct, withhold the perpetrators’ identities and expect Nigerians to accept ignorance as an excuse. He must account for this failure now.

“INEC must not quietly ‘clean up’ the register and bury the evidence. The allegation that more than 20 million AI generated images may be involved demands an independent forensic audit. Preserve every voter record, image file, access log and audit trail. Let accredited independent experts, political parties, civil society and credible international observers examine the evidence. No disputed record should be certified until the audit is complete.

“INEC has also ignored opposition parties’ demand to disclose the companies contracted to produce sensitive election materials. That secrecy is incompatible with a credible election. If the APC government knows who is handling these materials and what protocols apply, opposition parties must receive the same information. Publish the contractors’ identities and explain the safeguards governing their work.

“If INEC refuses to disclose the truth, we will go to court and compel it. Every official found to have tampered with the register must be prosecuted.”

Atiku called on opposition leaders and the international community to demand an independent audit, full disclosure and accountability. He accused President Tinubu’s government of enabling the crisis by allowing INEC to evade scrutiny.

INEC has no right to demand trust while concealing evidence and shielding those responsible. Name the culprits, expose the contractors and submit the register and election materials to independent scrutiny. Until then, its assurances are worthless. The credibility of the 2027 election is on the line.

Signed:
Phrank Shaibu
Director, Strategic Communication.
African Democratic Congress, Presidential Campaign Council.
30th October, 2026

AFCON To Return To Two-Year Cycle After CAF U-Turn by BlackViper(op): 3:12pm
The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf).

In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review.

Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient.

"The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.

The biennial hosting of Afcon has long caused issues with the football calendar, with the vast majority of recent tournaments held midway through the European club season.

Fifa's expanded 32-team Club World Cup was held in June and July last year, which also forced Caf to opt for mid-season dates.

The next Afcon will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament, followed by editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no tournament in 2030 because of the World Cup.

The dramatic 2025 Afcon final saw Senegal crowned champions before they were stripped of their title three months later in favour of Morocco.

item.content:encoded:
The Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State has dismissed reports alleging that the name of its governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, was missing from the list of candidates released by the Independent National Electoral Commission.

The party described the reports as false and misleading, accusing those behind them of attempting to create confusion within its ranks ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, 2026, and signed by its State Publicity Secretary, Kayode Adebayo, the PDP said there was no official publication or update on INEC’s website confirming Adebutu’s purported exclusion.

The party also stated that INEC had not issued any official statement or held a press briefing announcing the alleged exclusion of Adebutu or the publication of a list containing the name of another individual identified as Patanmi from Gombe State.

The statement, titled “Re: Purported Exclusion of Hon. (Dr.) Oladipupo Adebutu from INEC List — A Fabrication by Political Jobbers,” described the report as an attempt by political opponents to undermine the PDP candidate.

“The said report is false, unfounded, unverified and a figment of the imagination of its mischievous authors,” the party said.

The PDP maintained that Adebutu remained its authentic candidate for the Ogun State governorship election, expressing confidence that his name would appear on the ballot in line with the relevant constitutional provisions, the Electoral Act and INEC guidelines.

The party urged its supporters, members and the general public to disregard the reports and remain focused on its political activities.

It added that the party remained united and committed to its preparations for the forthcoming election, insisting that the alleged controversy would not distract its members.

As of the time of the statement, the PDP said it had not seen any official INEC publication confirming the reported exclusion.

item.content:encoded:
The Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee has invited applications for the 2027 award of the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria, with private legal practitioners required to pay a non-refundable processing fee of N5m and government-employed lawyers N2.5m.

The committee said the application portal would open on November 1, 2026, directing all candidates to complete the application process online and comply with its document submission requirements and deadlines.

PUNCH Online had reported Wednesday that Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee invited applications for the 2027 conferment of the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

Here are 10 things prospective applicants need to know about the exercise.

1. Applications open on November 11
The LPPC said its application portal would open to the public at 12am on November 1, 2026.

Applications are to be processed through its official portal, www.lppconline.com.

2. Private legal practitioners will pay N5m
The committee fixed the non-refundable processing fee for private legal practitioners at N5m.

3. Government-employed lawyers will pay N2.5m

Legal practitioners employed by the government are required to pay a non-refundable fee of N2.5m.

4. Payment must be made into designated bank accounts
Applicants are required to pay directly into either of the committee’s designated accounts:

– Zenith Bank: 1014103141

– Guaranty Trust Bank: 0213662834

5. Proof of payment must be uploaded
Candidates must upload evidence of payment to the online portal for verification.

According to the notice, the LPPC Secretariat will send a confirmation email after verification, allowing applicants to continue with the process.

6. All supporting documents must be uploaded online
Applicants seeking the rank through advocacy or academia must upload clear and legible scanned copies of all mandatory and supporting documents through the portal.

7. Academic applicants have additional requirements
Candidates applying through the academic category must submit seven physical photocopies each of their curriculum vitae and impact statement, in addition to the required flash drives.

8. Every applicant must submit five flash drives
The committee directed all applicants to provide five flash drives containing copies of their completed application forms downloaded from the portal and all mandatory and supporting documents uploaded during the application process.

9. Online applications close on January 31, 2027
The deadline for completing online applications is midnight on January 31, 2027. Applicants are advised to complete their submissions before the deadline to avoid technical or procedural complications.

10. Flash drives must arrive by February 1, 2027
The five flash drives must be delivered to the LPPC Secretariat before 4pm on February 1, 2027.

The committee warned that applications that do not comply with its guidelines or are submitted after the prescribed deadlines will be rejected and treated as non-submissions.

The notice was signed by the Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court of Nigeria and Secretary of the LPPC, Kabir Eniola Akanbi.

Applicants seeking clarification may contact the secretariat through lppcsecretariat@courts.gov.ng.

Twenty years after their daughter, sister, aunt and niece mysteriously left home and never returned, the family of late Chief Augustine Nwosu Maduka of Umuru Village, Ebenesi, Nnobi, in Idemili South Local Government Area of Anambra State, has decided and also announced plans to hold a funeral for her, despite still not knowing her whereabouts or what happened to her.

The missing woman, identified as Miss Nneka Nwosu, reportedly left...
item.content:encoded:
By Izunna Okafor, Awka

Twenty years after their daughter, sister, aunt and niece mysteriously left home and never returned, the family of late Chief Augustine Nwosu Maduka of Umuru Village, Ebenesi, Nnobi, in Idemili South Local Government Area of Anambra State, has decided and also announced plans to hold a funeral for her, despite still not knowing her whereabouts or what happened to her.

The missing woman, identified as Miss Nneka Nwosu, reportedly left home on December 31, 2006, at the age of 22, and has neither returned nor been found anywhere since then, leaving her family in prolonged anguish, uncertainty and years of fruitless efforts to locate her.

In a funeral announcement released by the family, the relatives described the past two decades as years of pain, sorrow, prayers, tears and unfulfilled hopes, recounting how they had continued to expect Nneka to one day walk back into her father's compound.

According to the emotional account accompanying the funeral announcement, the family had spent a fortune searching for her and pursuing different leads, including falling victim to people who allegedly took advantage of their desperation by claiming to know how to help them find her.

The family also recalled that their grandmother, Chiugo, died in December 2007 while still waiting for Nneka's return, while their father, Nze Chinemelu, also reportedly died in December 2012 without seeing his daughter again.

Recounting how much had changed in the family since her disappearance, the relatives disclosed that the five brothers who had no children as at that 2006 she left, were now fathers to 22 children, while four more children had also been added to the households of her sisters.

They further noted that the brothers, who were then young and struggling to establish themselves, had since made names for themselves, while their father's compound had undergone significant changes over the years, developments they wished Nneka could return to witness.

The family lamented that, beyond the emotional pain of her disappearance, they had also endured mockery from people who taunted them and repeatedly asked about the whereabouts of their sister.

Explaining the decision to proceed with the funeral, the family said tradition demanded that a person who had remained missing for 20 years be given a befitting burial, adding that they had resolved to fulfil the traditional rites despite the uncertainty surrounding her fate.

However, the family made an emotional appeal to Nneka to return home if she was still alive and had only been staying away from them. They also expressed hope that if she was being held somewhere against her will, God would set her free and bring her back to the family.

The relatives further prayed that if she was no longer alive, her soul would find eternal rest, while expressing their enduring desire to see her again, even after two decades of searching and waiting.

The funeral arrangements announced by the family indicate that a vigil Mass will hold on Friday, November 27, 2026, at the compound of late Chief Augustine Nwosu's family in Umuru, Ebenesi, Nnobi, at 5pm.

The funeral Mass is scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the same family compound by 10am, while the Thanksgiving and Outing Mass will take place on Sunday, November 29, at St. Paul Catholic Church, Umuru, Ebenato, Ebenesi, Nnobi, at 10am.

The funeral announcement was signed on behalf of the family by Mr. Chukwudi Nwosu, Mr. Azubuike Nwosu, Mr. Okwudili Nwosu, Mr. Obinna Nwosu and Mr. Oliver Nwosu.

Even as the family prepares to observe the traditional and religious rites, they further reiterated their appeal for Nneka's return open, expressing hope that wherever she may be, she could still find her way back home.

Ogala, who is facing charges bordering on alleged cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor, expressed remorse before Justice...
item.content:encoded:
Nollywood actress Doris Ogala, on Friday, knelt down before a Federal High Court in Lagos to apologise to the court over her unruly behaviour during an earlier sitting.

She was, however, returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre after the court reserved ruling on her bail application till November 6.

Ogala, who is facing charges bordering on alleged cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor, expressed remorse before Justice Akintayo Aluko, promising not to repeat the conduct that disrupted proceedings at the previous sitting.

The actress, who had been remanded at the correctional centre following her arraignment on Wednesday, personally appealed to the judge, saying she regretted her actions and never expected to find herself in prison custody.

She said, “I am very sorry, my Lord. I apologise for my bad behaviour. I have never been to prison before and I wasn’t expecting that I would do that.

“I regret my actions and I apologise to my Lord. I tender my apologies wholeheartedly. Sorry, this will never happen again going forward.”

Her apology followed the judge’s expression of displeasure over her unruly behaviour on Wednesday, after she was remanded.

Ogala allegedly shouted and sang in the courtroom, disrupting proceedings and forcing the court to rise.

Justice Aluko said her conduct prevented the court from hearing more than seven other cases scheduled for that day.

The judge said he had considered committing the actress for contempt on the day of the incident but decided against it, despite believing that her conduct warranted punishment.

He said, “She should have been given some form of imprisonment, right, on that day, but I kept my cool and I rose.”

The judge further said the actress could have received at least two months’ imprisonment for obstructing court proceedings.

Expressing his displeasure, Aluko said, “Why do you have to start shouting and start singing in the open court? You conducted yourself in a manner that forced the court to rise. That’s what you did, and it’s already recorded.”

He also faulted the defence counsel for failing to begin his address on the bail application by not acknowledging the incident and explaining the defendant’s conduct to the court.

The judge recalled that he had personally directed an accelerated consideration of the bail application, explaining that he had taken steps to ensure that it was heard within 48 hours.

He expressed disappointment that the Wednesday disruption occurred despite the court’s efforts to give the matter accelerated attention.

Ogala’s counsel, Marshal Abubakar, also apologised to the judge, describing the incident as regrettable and assuring the court that such conduct was not consistent with his client’s character.

He said he had known the defendant for some time and did not expect her to behave in that manner.


Following the apologies, the court proceeded to hear arguments on the bail application.

Moving the application, Abubakar urged the court to admit his client to bail, arguing that the prosecution had effectively acknowledged her entitlement to bail by proposing conditions for her release in its counter-affidavit.

He submitted that the prosecution’s position showed that it was not opposed to the defendant being released but was concerned about the conditions attached to her release.

According to him, where the prosecution accepts that a defendant may be admitted to bail, the court should exercise its discretion judicially and impose reasonable conditions.

He argued that bail conditions should not be unnecessarily restrictive, urging the judge to consider the circumstances of the case and the applicable provisions of the law.

The defence counsel also cited judicial authorities in support of his argument that bail conditions should be reasonable and should not undermine the right of an accused person to liberty pending trial.


However, the prosecution, led by Tolulope Mokolu, urged the court to impose stringent conditions on the actress, particularly in view of concerns about her activities on social media.

The prosecution argued that Ogala’s continued use of social media could negatively affect witnesses and potentially interfere with the administration of justice.

He maintained that although the defendant enjoyed the constitutional rights to freedom of speech and expression, such rights were not absolute and must be exercised within the limits of the law.


Mokolu therefore urged the court to restrict her contact with witnesses and their addresses and prevent her from making social media publications capable of influencing witnesses or undermining the proceedings.

The prosecution further argued that any breach of the proposed bail conditions should attract appropriate sanctions.

After listening to the submissions of both parties, Justice Aluko reserved ruling on the bail application till November 6, 2026.

Ogala was subsequently returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre, where she will remain pending the court’s decision on her bail application.

The actress was arraigned on Wednesday by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation on three counts bordering on alleged cyberbullying, cyberstalking and attempted extortion involving Pastor Okafor.

Prosecution counsel, Tolulope Mokolu, alleged that Ogala committed the offences between September 2024 and March 2026.

Mokolu told the court that the actress allegedly published nude and intimate photographs of Okafor on her social media accounts without his consent, exposing him to embarrassment, emotional distress and reputational damage.

She pleaded not guilty to the charges.

In an interview with Ogala’s counsel, Marshal Abubakar, said he will petition the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, to withdraw the criminal charges against his client, describing the case as a private dispute between former lovers.

Abubakar disclosed this on Friday while reacting to the decision of the Federal High Court in Lagos to reserve ruling on Ogala’s bail application till November 6, 2026.

Speaking after the proceedings, Abubakar said he believed the prosecution of Ogala was an infringement on her fundamental rights, insisting that the dispute which led to the charges arose from a failed relationship.

He said, “I strongly believe that the arrest of Doris Ogala, the investigation as far as this matter is concerned, and the subsequent filing of charges against her are an affront to her fundamental rights.

“The subject matter that led to this entire transaction in this matter was purely a matter between a boyfriend and a girlfriend. Where former lovers fell apart, and one of the lovers felt cheated, and she reacted through the platform that she has.”

The lawyer stated that the state should not ordinarily involve itself in such a private dispute, adding that Nigerians had the right to express their grievances.

He said, “As far as I am concerned, these are private issues and private matters that the state ordinarily should not involve itself with. Nigerians have a fundamental right to express their grievances and express themselves in manners that they deem fit and appropriate.

“The idea of criminalising free speech in this country has been contemptuous. We will never shy away from condemning the idea behind having a law that seeks to, or has, a chilling effect on Nigerians as it relates to how they should express themselves in a democracy.”


Abubakar further said that individuals who felt defamed by another person’s statements should seek redress through civil proceedings rather than using law enforcement agencies to arrest and prosecute their critics.

According to him, democracy accommodates dissent and criticism, even where the expressions are considered offensive.

“Democracy accepts dissent. Democracy accepts even vulgar abuses where a person feels strongly defamed by the utterances of a person who has exercised his right under the law as it relates to their fundamental rights to express themselves.

“The natural remedy for such a person is to file a civil matter under the tort of defamation. If I feel strongly defamed by the utterances of a particular person, what I naturally would want to do is to go to court, where my integrity and reputation can be put on the line,” he said.


The lawyer maintained that approaching law enforcement agencies to arrest individuals over criticism or insults had no place in a democratic society.

He also called for the removal of provisions of the Cybercrimes Act which, according to him, criminalise free speech.

Abubakar recalled that in 2022, challenges were brought before the courts against provisions of the Cybercrimes Act 2015, particularly Section 24, which he said had been declared unconstitutional in two separate judgments for violating the right to freedom of expression and provisions of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights.

He said the National Assembly subsequently amended the Act in 2024 to address concerns surrounding the criminalisation of free speech.

However, he alleged that security agencies had continued to apply the law without adequately reflecting the amendments.

The lawyer accused some influential individuals and public officials of using law enforcement agencies to intimidate critics, arguing that such practices undermined democratic freedoms.

He said, “Today, when you insult somebody who is a man of means, or you insult a government official who has done something very bad, the same government official will simply approach the police and give them money to arrest and detain such an individual. In a democracy, this should never be.”

Asked whether he would formally challenge the prosecution, having appeared before the court, Abubakar said he intended to write directly to the Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, urging him to intervene.

He said, “It is also my honest belief that this matter should be discontinued and the charges withdrawn. In that regard, I will be filing an application to the Minister of Justice and the Attorney-General to withdraw this charge because it ought not to have been filed in the first place.”

He added that the request would be made in the interest of justice, insisting that the dispute should not proceed as a criminal case against a Nigerian citizen.

Katsina: 64 Students Hospitalised After Deworming Medication as Teachers Face Abuse Allegations

64 Katsina students hospitalised after taking deworming medication, teachers accused of beating pupils who complained of illness

At least 64 students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, Katsina State, have reportedly been hospitalised after developing complications following the administration of medication for schistosomiasis, a parasitic worm infection.

According to security analyst Zagazola Makama, the incident occurred on October 26, 2026, when several students began experiencing vomiting, dizziness and abdominal pain after taking the medication.

Some of the affected students were reportedly unconscious by the time they arrived at the hospital.

The students were taken to General Amadi Rimi Specialist Hospital in Batagarawa, Katsina General Hospital and Turai Yar'Adua Hospital for medical attention.


The report also alleged that some teachers physically assaulted students who complained of feeling unwell, accusing them of pretending to be sick rather than seeking medical assistance for them.

Makama called on the Katsina State Government and the Ministries of Education and Health to investigate the incident, including the type of medication administered, its dosage and whether proper medical supervision was provided.

He also urged authorities to investigate the allegations against the teachers and take appropriate action if they are found responsible.

item.content:encoded:
FIFA U-17 WWC: Flamingos Beat Mexico 2-1, Set Up Quarterfinal Clash With Venezuela

Nigeria’s Flamingos have reached the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 women’s World Cup after defeating Mexico 2-1 in Thursday’s round of 16 tie, completesports.com reports.

Oluebube Umejiaku put the Flamingos ahead late in the first half while Mary Dunstan doubled the lead with less than 20 minutes left in the second half.

Emily Delgado pulled a goal back for Mexico deep in added time but the Flamingos held on to advance to the last eight.

The Flamingos will now take on Venezuela in the quarterfinal on Sunday, November 1st. Venezuela reached the quarterfinal after edging out Germany 1-0.

Citlalli Reyes made the first attempt on goal just four minutes into the game but failed to find the back of the net.

Three minutes later Reyes went close again but to broke the deadlock for her side.

In the 20th minute the Flamingos had their first chance on goal but Oluwakemi Adegbuyi could not convert her chance, while Umejiaku also could not find the back of the net on 26 minutes.

With five minutes left in the first half Umejiaku put the Flamimgos 1-0 ahead as she took advantage of a poor interception by a Mexican player, dribbled her marker inside the box and fired past the keeper.

The Flamingos edged the early part of the second half and almost went 2-0 up on 48 minutes up Queen Joseph’s attempt was cleared away.

On the hour mark a dangerous corner kick from a Flamingos player deflected off a Mexican player but the keeper was quick to stop the ball from going in.

Some minutes later Flamingos continued to create scoring chances and were almost rewarded but Tosin Rafiu’s long lob was stopped from going in by the Mexican keeper.

Then in the 71st minute, Dunstan made it 2-0 as she volleyed into the back of the net after the keeper failed to properly punch away a cross into the box.

The goal was reviewed for a possible foul on a Mexican keeper in the build up to the goal but it was finally given.

With two minutes left a Mexico player Mia Urbano tried a long range strike but Flamingos keeper Jane Ijirigho tipped it against the bar.

But in the 10th minute of added time Delgado scored for Mexico as she controlled a poor clearance from a corner kick and fired a left-foot shot into the net.

The goal by Mexico turned out to be a consolation goal as the Flamingos held on to advance into the quarterfinals.
